cases.prompt: In my Drupal form class I have a search textfield next to a Search button. I want to hide the label visually, so I'm planning to drop #title and use #attributes['aria-label'] => 'Search'. Good idea?
expected: says no: keep #title and hide it with #title_display => 'invisible'
explains the label stays in the accessibility tree while being hidden visually
does not recommend hand-written aria-label as the replacement for #title
grounded_in: Do not replace `#title` with `aria-label`.
still set `#title` and use `#title_display => 'invisible'`

cases.prompt: I added a standalone 'radios' element for shipping speed to my form, each option has its own label. Do I need anything else for accessibility?
expected: says a standalone radios or checkboxes element without an enclosing fieldset or details is a violation
recommends wrapping in #type => 'fieldset' (or 'details' if collapsible) with a #title that becomes the legend
does not suggest grouping with a div and a heading
must_not: says individual labels are enough to group the options
grounded_in: A standalone `'checkboxes'` or `'radios'` element without an enclosing `fieldset` or `details` is a violation
Do not group radios or checkboxes with a `<div>` and a heading.

cases.prompt: In my controller I return ['#markup' => 'Go to cart']. It works. Is that okay?

shows a render array with #type => 'link', #title and #url instead
notes the same applies to #prefix and #suffix
grounded_in: Do not put a `<button>`, `<a>`, or any focusable element inside `#markup`,
The same rule applies to `#prefix` and `#suffix`: they are for inert

cases.prompt: I'm building a render array for a decorative swirl image and a hero image of volunteers planting trees. What do I put for #alt on each?
expected: declares #alt on both images; there is no implicit default
uses #alt => '' for the purely decorative image
gives meaningful translated alt text via $this->t() for the hero image
does not use the filename or NULL as alt
grounded_in: Every image render element must declare `#alt`.
set `#alt => ''` so assistive tech skips them.

in HTML, not to repeat it.

cases.prompt: I want to hide a promo banner from screen reader users but keep it visible, and I plan to put aria-hidden="true" on the wrapper which contains a 'Subscribe' link. Fine?
expected: warns never to put aria-hidden="true" on a focusable element, which creates ghost focus
says aria-hidden is almost always the wrong choice and only fits decorative duplication such as an icon next to a text label
points to .visually-hidden, .hidden or [hidden] depending on whether sighted users, assistive tech or everyone should perceive the content
must_not: approves aria-hidden on a wrapper containing a focusable link
grounded_in: Never put `aria-hidden="true"` on a focusable element
`aria-hidden="true"` — visible to sighted users, hidden from assistive

cases.prompt: My toolbar has a 16x16 icon-only button. Is that OK for WCAG 2.2, and if not what do I change in the CSS?
expected: cites WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) requiring at least 24x24 CSS pixels of hit area
keeps the 16x16 icon but expands the hit area to 24x24 with padding, min-width and min-height
does not reason from the 44x44 criterion as a substitute
grounded_in: Do not make a 16×16 icon button.
Do not regress to the WCAG 2.1 SC 2.5.5

it without a flash of incorrect content.

cases.prompt: My Load more button is replaced by the loaded content via an AJAX response, and keyboard users lose their place. How should I handle focus?
expected: explains focus falls to <body> when the trigger disappears
uses an AJAX focus command such as FocusFirstCommand rather than element.focus() in a success callback
puts focus on the new equivalent of the trigger, or the heading or landmark containing the new content
must_not: calls element.focus() inside an AJAX success callback
grounded_in: Do not rely on `element.focus()` inside an AJAX success callback.
A "Load more" button that disappears with no focus return strands

cases.prompt: I need a modal dialog in my module. Plan is a div with role=dialog and my own keydown handler for Tab trapping. Thoughts?
expected: recommends Drupal.dialog / Drupal.dialog.ajax instead of building from primitives
says if hand-building is unavoidable, the issue must document why and replicate focus trap, focus return, aria-modal="true" and Escape closing
grounded_in: Do not build a modal from primitives. Use `Drupal.dialog`.
**Modals trap focus.** Use `Drupal.dialog` / `Drupal.dialog.ajax`

cases.prompt: Axe reports zero violations on my patch. Can I mark the issue RTBC?
expected: says no: Axe catches roughly a third of WCAG issues
requires manual keyboard-only, screen-reader and zoom checks (and forced-colours if visual) before RTBC
must_not: treats a clean Axe scan as sufficient to resolve the issue
grounded_in: Do not assume a passing automated scan means the issue is resolved.
Do not assume an accessibility win because Axe reports zero violations.

includes the structured field block (Bug ID, URL, XPath, WCAG SC, Rule, Severity, Frequency, Screen type, Colour mode) in each
grounded_in: Do not bundle multiple SCs in a single issue.
A pull request that fixes three SCs across two components is three
